title: What Sub-Nanometer Transistors Is
provenance: Public research knowledge: documented developments, published research, and established technical references. Real, fact-checked records.
description: Sub-nanometer transistors are switching devices with gate lengths at or below one nanometer — the end of classical scaling. They use gate-all-around nanosheets, 2D materials like molybdenum disulfide, or carbon nanotubes to keep switching crisply when silicon fins can shrink no further. This record is the entry point of the teaching ladder for Sub-Nanometer Transistors: start here, then move through the research state, the specifications, the public developments, the open challenges, and finally each piece needed to build it.
key_points: Sub-Nanometer Transistors in one line: Sub-nanometer transistors are switching devices with gate lengths at or below one nanometer — the end of classical scaling.
Why it matters: They are the last rung of Moore's law: without them, transistor density stalls and computing efficiency plateaus..
Where it is used: future CPUs, mobile SoCs, AI accelerators, ultra-low-power edge chips..
Ladder rank 1 — the foundation. Everything else builds on this.

t: Current Research State of Sub-Nanometer Transistors
title: Current Research State of Sub-Nanometer Transistors
provenance: Public research knowledge: documented developments, published research, and established technical references. Real, fact-checked records.
description: Labs demonstrated 1nm-class transistors with carbon nanotubes and 2D materials, and industry roadmaps show gate-all-around evolving to complementary FETs (CFETs) stacking n- and p-devices. TSMC, Intel, and Samsung race on angstrom-class nodes. The gap: manufacturing 2D materials at wafer scale with transistor-grade uniformity. Research moves in three waves: laboratory proof of concept, scaled prototypes under controlled conditions, and field trials. Sub-Nanometer Transistors currently sits at the stage described above, and the pieces records show what each wave still needs.
